verdicts.factCheck: I fetched the Sourcify record for 0x6fb00a180781e75f87e2b690af0196baa77c7e7c on 22 November 2026. It reports a full creation and runtime match, contract name Orchestrator, solc 0.4.24. rebase() is external, its first statement is require(msg.sender == tx.origin), it then calls policy.rebase() and runs a list of downstream calls, and it reverts if one of them fails. The comment above it says contracts are guarded from calling to avoid flash loan attacks on liquidity providers. On chain at block 26472347 through the RPC in networks.json (reth v2.11.0): AMPL.monetaryPolicy() is 0x1b228a749077b8e307c5856ce62ef35d96dca2ea, policy.orchestrator() is the Orchestrator and Orchestrator.policy() points back, AMPL.balanceOf(PoolManager) is 16 base units, totalSupply is 1527834484102092 base units (9 decimals), inRebaseWindow() is 0, lastRebaseTimestampSec is 1795312800, the interval, offset and window length are 86400, 7200 and 1200 seconds, epoch is 2695 and the Orchestrator holds 4 downstream calls. eth_config reports fork id 0x07c9462e with activation time 1767747671. All of this matches the finding. The finding says it did not simulate a delegated account. I did, with eth_simulateV1 on the latest block (26472347 or a few blocks later) and a block time override of 1795399230, which lies inside the next rebase window. A call to rebase() from an account without code succeeded with 11 logs and 343,310 gas. The same call routed through a 51 byte forwarding contract placed by state override reverted after 24,029 gas with empty data, which is the origin check. An account whose code was overridden to the EIP-7702 designator 0xef0100 followed by the forwarder address then sent a transaction to itself. Its delegated code called rebase() and the call succeeded with the same 11 logs and 345,901 gas. Without the time override the plain account and the delegated account both reverted deeper in the call (43,028 and 45,618 gas) and the forwarder contract still stopped at 24,029 gas. A delegated account therefore passes the guard while it runs code, on the node that serves mainnet today. EIP-7702 (status Final) says in the section on self-sponsoring, lines 299 to 319, that the EIP breaks the invariant that msg.sender == tx.origin only happens in the topmost execution frame, and that the protection against atomic sandwich attacks such as flash loans would be broken. Lines 554 to 559 repeat this. The amount is zero today. In my simulated rebase the total supply and the PoolManager balance of 16 base units did not change. The last real rebase, at block 26467574, logged a supply change of 0 at a market rate of 1.2473 against a target of 1.2708. I reran the other triggers the finding names: Comptroller.claimComp(PoolManager) from an unrelated account succeeded and left the COMP balance at 5422.05, and Olympus staking rebase() succeeded and left the sOHM balance at 249.389779689, with epoch() reporting nothing to distribute. The Blockscout token list for the PoolManager had 66,563 rows at my fetch and shows the AMPL row with value 16. I found no primary source that contradicts the finding. I did not rerun the CometRewards claim and I did not read the source of the deployed monetary policy, which emits a newer rebase event than the policy code bundled with the Orchestrator source.
verdicts.codeCheck: sync has no modifier. For a non-zero currency it reads balanceOf(PoolManager) and stores the currency and that value in transient storage (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/types/Currency.sol:90-96, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32). _settle reads the synced currency, rejects msg.value for a non-zero currency (line 356), computes paid as the current balance minus the stored value with checked subtraction (358-360), clears the synced currency (361) and credits the named recipient with paid (364). Nothing ties the rise to a transfer made by the settler. take debits msg.sender and then transfers (291-297). unlock calls unlockCallback on msg.sender and afterwards requires the count of open deltas to be zero (104-114). A credit of g from settle and a debit of g from take under the same currency and account cancel in _accountDelta (368-378), so the count check passes. I looked for a guard that would stop the sequence and found none. The msg.value check does not apply because no value is sent. The synced currency check in collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:48-52) only limits the fee controller. The int128 cast in settle and take (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-59) limits an amount to 2^127 - 1, far above the AMPL supply. AMPL returns true from transfer, so the return data check in Currency.transfer passes (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). A search of the non-test sources shows that balanceOfSelf is called only at PoolManager.sol:285 and 359, so pool, position and claim accounting never see a rebase, and a positive one is credited to whoever brackets it. A negative rebase makes line 360 revert, so only gains can be booked. donate debits the donor and raises fee growth for in-range liquidity (src/PoolManager.sol:256-276, src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480), so the mitigation described is available. sync is not the only route. take lets the caller hold the whole pooled AMPL balance for a nominal debit (291-297). If the rebase runs while the caller holds the tokens, the caller repays the nominal amount through sync, transfer and settle and keeps the growth. The result is the same as the bracket in the finding.
verdicts.corrections: The actor value unprivileged is right: every step is open to any account, and the pooled token and the pool are not made by the attacker. The assumptions should also list A5, because a take of the pooled balance before the rebase followed by a nominal repayment gives the same gain without a sync before the rebase. A change that only restricted sync would leave that route open. The supports text for the EIP source says the broken invariant is that msg.sender == tx.origin implies an account without code. The EIP words it as the check being true only in the topmost execution frame, and it says the use of the check to ensure that msg.sender is an EOA is unaffected. The conclusion for the Orchestrator guard is the same. The preconditions should say that recent rebases changed supply by zero (block 26467574, and my simulation of the next window), so a gain needs a market rate outside the policy's deviation band as well as a pool that holds AMPL. With 16 base units held, the gain rounds to zero today. The Blockscout row count was 66,563 at my fetch. Severity stays medium on the scale: the loss is limited to pools that hold an elastic supply or reward pushing token, and no such pool holds a material balance today.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Native payout (P1) to contracts that book incoming ETH to the sender: WETH9, Lido stETH, frxETHMinter, EntryPoint v0.6, v0.7 and v0.8, the OptimismPortal of OP Mainnet and Base, and the TokenJar. Does the caller end up owing less than what left, with or without a sync and settle around the payout?
clearedSpotChecks.note: Code: take books the full native debit before the value call (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295, src/types/Currency.sol:45-53), and a credit under another currency id is only the measured rise since the latest sync (358-360, 364). The two legs are booked under two ids, so a recipient that pays the PoolManager back in a token at the market rate or worse gives the caller nothing. On chain with eth_simulateV1 at the latest block on 22 November 2026 (26472347 or a few blocks later) and the PoolManager as sender: 1 ETH with empty calldata raised WETH9.balanceOf(PoolManager) by exactly 1e18 (574.79 WETH before), raised stETH.balanceOf(PoolManager) by 1e18 - 1, and raised EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7 balanceOf(PoolManager) from 0 to 1e18. transfer(address,uint256) from the PoolManager reverts at both EntryPoints, so that ledger credit cannot be paid out. I did not rerun frxETHMinter, EntryPoint v0.8, the portals or the TokenJar, and my calls had tx.origin equal to the PoolManager, which does not matter for WETH9, Lido and EntryPoint.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Faces on mainnet: can one balance be reached under two currency ids so that a payment is credited twice or one id drains the other. Checked ETH against WETH9, tokens with two entry points (TUSD and SNX), and a ledger credited by a value transfer (EntryPoint).
clearedSpotChecks.note: Code: there is one synced currency slot and one reserves slot, every sync of a non-zero currency writes both, and sync(address(0)) clears only the currency, so a stale reserves value cannot be paired with a currency again without a fresh balance read (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32). A native credit needs the synced currency to be zero and an ERC-20 credit rejects msg.value (353-356). settle and settleFor are the only payable functions in the non-test sources and there is no receive or fallback function. The research left the second entry points untested. I tested them with eth_simulateV1 at the latest block on 22 November 2026 (26472347 or a few blocks later): balanceOf(PoolManager) and transfer from the PoolManager both revert at the old TUSD address 0x8dd5fbCe2F6a956C3022bA3663759011Dd51e73E and at the old SNX proxy 0xC011A72400E58ecD99Ee497CF89E3775d4bd732F (the latter with the message Only the proxy can call), while the current SNX proxy moves exactly 1e18 for a 1e18 transfer. Neither token is reachable under a second currency id today, which closes the first part of the open lead on this point.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether the public reward and rebase triggers that exist today for tokens the PoolManager holds move value that a caller could book: Compound v2 claimComp, Compound v3 CometRewards.claim, Olympus staking rebase, OUSD and OETH vault rebase, Aave aToken growth.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Remeasured with eth_simulateV1 at the latest block on 22 November 2026 (26472347 or a few blocks later). claimComp(PoolManager) from an unrelated account succeeds and leaves the COMP balance unchanged. Olympus staking rebase() succeeds and leaves the sOHM balance unchanged, and epoch() reports 0 to distribute. OUSD.rebaseState(PoolManager) is 1 and nonRebasingCreditsPerToken(PoolManager) is 1e18, so the 20,053 OUSD do not grow when the vault rebases; I read state 1 as the non-rebasing state from the fixed credits value and did not fetch the OUSD source. The aToken argument holds from the code side: a credit needs a rise inside one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), time-based interest does not change within a transaction, and a caller who pays a flash loan premium to move the index gets back only the PoolManager's share of it. I did not rerun the Comet claim or the OETH vault call. The largest rebasing balance, 80.47 stETH, changes only in the oracle report, which the earlier stETH finding covers.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether a zero amount call made by the PoolManager, either take(address(0), X, 0) with empty calldata or take(X, to, 0) as X.transfer(to, 0), changes a balance the PoolManager holds on the targets swept, and whether the PoolManager can be made to call itself.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Code: _accountDelta returns at once for a zero delta (src/PoolManager.sol:369), so a zero amount take books nothing and still makes the call (291-297). I computed the selectors of all 33 external and public functions of the PoolManager, including the public mappings and the solmate Owned functions, and compared them with transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(address), unlockCallback(bytes) and the ten IHooks selectors. There is no collision, and the non-test sources have no receive or fallback function, so every call the PoolManager can be made to send to its own address reverts. I did not repeat the zero amount calls on chain.
